clue.text: Intend — in craze for melody — to find stardom

indicators.note: the word for intend is placed inside the word for craze, as the clue says

parts.note: a craze is a passing fad
to intend is to mean
taken as written
a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: A musician hopes a catchy, trendy tune will make them a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom brings celebrity and riches, the pair named in the familiar phrase.

clue.text: For influence, write the thing with Hemingway's ending

parts.note: to author something is to write it
it stands for a thing already mentioned

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here of the novelist's surname

explanation.surface: Advice to a would-be writer: to have impact, write the thing and end it like Hemingway.
explanation.definitionFit: Authority is power or sway over others, which is what influence means.

clue.text: Lassitude, as Lennon put it, oddly dismissive

indicators.note: dismissing the odd letters keeps only the second, fourth, sixth and so on of the words Lennon put it

explanation.surface: Lennon describes weariness in an offhand, oddly dismissive way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly dismissive' throws away letters 1, 3, 5... of LENNONPUTIT, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and weariness, a synonym for lassitude.

clue.text: Managed to see increase with share account

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that increases rises, so the word for managed is read upwards

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it; past tense ran
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A firm managed to raise its stake by sharing an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'increase' turns RAN upwards in this down entry, giving NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken or written account of events, a story told.

clue.text: Madagascan mammal first to find bones

indicators.note: the first letter is taken from the word find

parts.note: ossa is the Latin plural of os, a bone

explanation.surface: A Madagascan creature is the first to locate some bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The fossa is a cat-like carnivore found only on Madagascar.

clue.text: Getting jewellery put on rightly leads to conviction?

parts.note: rings are items of jewellery
something put on straight or correctly aligned is true, as in a door hung true

explanation.surface: Buying jewellery and wearing it properly might win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sounds convincing persuades the hearer, so it produces belief or conviction.

clue.text: Sons name desert leader of Muslims, having run in extremist

indicators.note: the letter for run goes inside what remains of the ruler's title
the letters for sons and name desert, or leave, the ruler's title

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim ruler
S is the abbreviation for son
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An extremist's sons give a desert ruler a name after running in.
explanation.walkthrough: S and N are the outer letters of SULTAN; 'desert' strips them to ULTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a hardliner or zealot.

clue.text: Extremely brave female leaves, having no listeners

indicators.note: the letter for female departs from the word for extremely brave

parts.note: fearless means utterly brave

explanation.surface: A very brave woman walks out, having no audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an outer-letters signal, but 'Extremely brave' is a whole synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears are what one listens with, so a creature lacking them has no organs of hearing.

clue.text: Fibres, excellent, fine and very much pushed back

indicators.note: the whole string is pushed backwards, read upward in this down entry

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI
F is the abbreviation for fine (on pencils)
far means very much, as in far better

explanation.surface: Fine, excellent fibres being pushed back hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is the fibre from palm leaves, used for weaving and tying.

clue.text: Performance taking place in West London district

parts.note: an act is a performance
an event that is on is happening

explanation.surface: A show is being staged in a West London neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district in the borough of Ealing, in the west of London.

clue.text: Arrest Ono brutally? One makes sympathetic noises

indicators.note: treating the words roughly, so their letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Police manhandle Yoko Ono while someone looks on with sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonator vibrates in sympathy with another source, physics' sympathetic vibration.

clue.text: Excessively ornate answer reveals keys location

parts.note: florid means overly elaborate

explanation.surface: An over-elaborate answer shows where the keys are.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida Keys are a chain of islands off the southern tip of the US state.

clue.text: Soften when wise man stores uranium

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left

indicators.note: the wise man holds the uranium symbol inside, as a store keeps goods

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A wise man softens his stance once he stockpiles uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage pain or feelings is to ease or soften them.

clue.text: Manx cat for example shows inner personality

indicators.note: the Manx cat famously has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cat is an example of an animal

explanation.surface: A tailless cat from the Isle of Man reveals its inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' reads as describing the cat but tells you to dock the tail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul, the unconscious personality.

clue.text: Greek leader soon to host contest millions attend

indicators.note: the word for soon holds the others inside it, like a host with guests

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
a game is a contest

explanation.surface: A Greek leader will soon stage a match watched by millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Organism spreads to consume upper-class twit

indicators.note: the mixed letters eat up the upper-class letter, taking it inside
the organism spreads out, its letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A spreading organism devours a posh fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, a fool or twit.

clue.text: Unfortunately son grew up in e-mail forum

indicators.note: things went badly for the letters, which are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, the son came of age chatting on an online discussion list.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsgroup is an internet discussion forum where messages are posted and shared.

clue.text: Give me old-fashioned stuff — a sensational piece!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of old are shaped or fashioned into a new order

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Someone asks for old-fashioned material and gets a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective, but it splits into fodder and the anagram signal 'fashioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational play with exaggerated characters and emotions.

clue.text: Soon Andy sent mad — no way out

indicators.note: Andy is driven crazy, so his letters go wild
out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: Andy is driven mad, with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very soon, at any moment.

clue.text: Approval from leader to admonish city council on trashy mail

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for city council

indicators.note: rubbishy, so the letters are trashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A leader admonishes the council over junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic praise and approval.

clue.text: The French in their way rejected Swiss scientist

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the reversed street word
rejected means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: their refers to the French; their word for street is rue
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French rejected a Swiss scientist in their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the French, so the way is the French street word; 'rejected' turns it to EUR before the article goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician and physicist.

clue.text: Recovery monies trickled down a little? Not quite!

parts.note: liquid that trickled down ran

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: some means a little

explanation.surface: Money for recovery barely trickled down at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the E of SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is money paid to recover a captive.

clue.text: HCE and ALP supply saint's holy locations

indicators.note: read as supple-y, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Joyce's HCE and ALP, from Finnegans Wake, provide a saint's shrines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb from supple, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapels are small places of worship, sacred buildings.

clue.text: Forest burning incessantly

indicators.note: read as in-cease-ant-ly: without ceasing becomes without its end, the last letter cut

parts.note: ardent means burning or passionate

explanation.surface: A forest is ablaze nonstop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incessantly' is read as endlessly: ARDENT loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden in Warwickshire is the setting of As You Like It.

clue.text: European succeeded three times around London area

indicators.note: the three letters sit around the London postcode

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, taken three times
W1 is the postcode of London's West End, written as WI

explanation.surface: A European made it big three times around central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss person is a European from Switzerland.

clue.text: Make merry to combine in mountain valley

indicators.note: the word for combine is placed inside the valley

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
to add things is to combine them

explanation.surface: Having fun by joining up in a mountain valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden someone is to make them happy or cheerful.

clue.text: Resin discovered in Camberwell

indicators.note: found inside the place name, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: Resin found in Camberwell, a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin.

clue.text: Mark in time a new dawn's dawn: nation reformed

indicators.note: the dawn of a word is its beginning, its first letter
the nation is reformed, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Commemorating a nation reborn at the dawn of a new era.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a tempo marking in music, telling the player the pace, or time.

clue.text: Get to vote against the party

parts.note: get can mean become or be, as in get angry
a vote against is a no

explanation.surface: Being urged to vote against a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vote against' is to be a no, a no-voter.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Bernard Shaw's piece with really nice chap on island

parts.note: a chap is a man
and means with or plus
super means excellent
the Isle of Man, known simply as Man

explanation.surface: A Shaw work featuring a lovely chap on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play of 1903 popularised the Nietzschean superhuman in English.
